title: Police capture suspected serial killer disguised as woman, carrying baby
summary: Brazilian police said they will reopen dozens of cases linked to a self-confessed serial killer who was arrested as he attempted to escape dressed as a woman and carrying a baby.
story: Brazilian police said Friday they had captured a suspected serial killer linked to at least 16 deaths since May, who was arrested while disguised as a woman and carrying a baby.
He claims to have killed more than four times that number.
The suspect was arrested Sunday after a 30-hour police manhunt in a forested area of Paraiba state in northeastern Brazil.
He was wearing a dress and long black wig, which police described as a disguise to evade capture. In a statement, they said he had been carrying a baby in his arms.
Images and video published by local media, including O Globo, showed the suspect with painted nails wearing a striped dress, a dark wig, women's sandals and sunglasses.
Police said the child he was carrying was not related to him. Police did not release details on the baby's condition.

"Although the suspect claimed involvement in 80 homicides, civil police have confirmed his participation in 16 killings in the region, 11 of which he confessed to during questioning," police told AFP.
The 16 homicides all took place since May. The identities of the victims and details of the killings have not been made public.
The suspect was identified by authorities as 33-year-old Jorlan Lopes da Silva, Record R7 reported.
The suspect evaded an earlier attempt to arrest him a few weeks ago after a confrontation with security forces, who consider him a member of an "ultra-violent" criminal group.
In a video of his interrogation obtained by AFP, the man said he acted alone and denied having ties to organized crime.
Instead, he claimed all his victims were "linked to the criminal world" and he was taking justice into his own hands in response to threats against himself and his family.
"I never acted against any family man, mother or working person," he said, denying being a "psychopath."
He said he had committed his first homicide at the age of 13.

After the earlier attempt to arrest the suspect, police seized bulletproof vests, the stock of a submachine gun and over 100 rounds of ammunition, which the man acknowledged were his during questioning. Two other men were arrested during the operation on suspicion of involvement in the crime, according to iG Último Segundo.
Under Brazilian law, he faces a maximum sentence of 40 years in prison, according to Record R7.
The region of Mulungu, where the killings took place, lies 1,553 miles north of Rio de Janeiro.

title: Trump touts plan for new U.S. base as Poland warns of risks from Russia
summary: Trump touts "major progress" on plans for a permanent U.S. Army base in Poland as the country's leader warns Russia's war on Ukraine could hit NATO soil.
story: Berlin — The U.S. has made "major progress" on plans to establish a permanent U.S. Army base in Poland, President Trump said Thursday in a social media post.

"If this goes ahead, the location will be announced very soon," Mr. Trump said in his Truth Social post, which was shared by the White House on X. He said the new base would be a "historic step" for the U.S.-Poland alliance.
Poland's government is likely to welcome the rhetoric as concern mounts over the possible spread of Russia's ongoing full-scale war on neighboring Ukraine to NATO territory.
A "real risk" of Russia's war on Ukraine spreading?

Prime Minister Donald Tusk spoke in Poland's parliament, hours before Mr. Trump's post, of a "real risk that drones or other types of projectiles will enter the territory of one or several countries on the [NATO] eastern flank and even cause destruction."

Citing unspecified intelligence, Tusk said Russia could portray such an incident — of which there are already numerous examples —   even if it is deliberate, as an accident in a bid to erode NATO's willingness to mount a joint response.

Tusk also referred to a new generation of jet-powered attack drones that Russia has been using to attack Ukraine. Compared to the propeller-driven weapons used for more than four years, the newer drones fly faster and at higher altitudes, making them more difficult to intercept.
Russia is also increasingly targeting Ukrainian infrastructure near the Polish border, Tusk said.

On Sunday, a Russian drone struck a passenger train inside Ukraine carrying foreign dignitaries on a visit, including senior European officials and former CIA Director David Petraeus, forcing them to evacuate just a few miles from the border with Poland.

"Maybe they didn't know that some Americans had been there, or maybe, oppositely, they knew, because I don't trust them," Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CBS News in an exclusive interview this week.
"I think that they knew," Zelenskyy added, calling it part of a Russian strategy to intimidate himself and other foreign leaders.
Another drone struck a truck at a nearby gas station. The drone impacts forced Poland's border guards to temporarily suspend cross-border traffic, evacuate people from vehicles and enhance security.
Poland hardens its border

Poland has also boosted its military preparedness. Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Tuesday that soldiers from an engineering regiment were reinforcing border guard infrastructure along the Polish-Ukrainian frontier.

According to the Polish Armed Forces, the measures include the installation of Hesco bastions —   wire and mesh structures filled with sand or gravel that are easy to set up as protective barriers —   along with new observation and guard posts.

Similar work has been confirmed at three border crossings, in Dorohusk, Medyka and Korczowa. The total number of additional Polish soldiers sent to the border has not been made public. Officials have said the measures should not be considered a general military mobilization or large-scale buildup, as they are intended specifically to reinforce and secure border infrastructure.

But Poland, and its European NATO allies, along with Ukraine and Russia, know a U.S. troop deployment —   especially a permanent one —   would be a step up in NATO's fortifications of its eastern flank.
Trump administration's "confusing" NATO stance

Mr. Trump's post on Thursday, in which he lauded "our Great U.S./Polish Alliance," was the latest twist in his administration's evolving plans and messaging around U.S. troop deployments that have kept close European allies guessing.

In May, Vice President JD Vance accused media outlets of "overreacting" to an announcement that a planned deployment of 4,000 U.S. forces to Poland had been canceled. Two days later, Mr. Trump announced that the deployment was not only going ahead, but that it would involve 5,000 troops.
"All's well that ends well," Poland's Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said at the time.
His Swedish counterpart, Maria Malmer Stenergard, called the U.S. position on joint defense under the nearly 80-year-old NATO alliance, "confusing indeed, and not always easy to navigate."
The roughly 10,000 U.S. forces currently stationed in Poland are there largely on a rotational basis.
In June, Defense Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz said the U.S. military was considering Poland's proposal to establish a permanent base, but that no final decision had been made.

Separately, the Pentagon has been conducting a broader review of U.S. troop deployments across Europe. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, in announcing the review in June, said the "era of freeriding" by America's NATO allies was over, accusing them of "shameful" inaction during the Iran war.
Kosiniak-Kamysz has named Poznań and Wrocław as potential locations for an American base, but no final location has been announced.

title: Princess Diana's brother claims Charles sounded "elated" after she died
summary: Princess Diana's brother claims in his book that then-Prince Charles "sounded giddily elated" right after his ex-wife died in a Paris car crash.
story: London — The brother of the late Princess Diana claims in his upcoming book that King Charles III, then Prince Charles, "sounded giddily elated — like a lottery winner," right after his ex-wife died in a Paris car crash in 1997.
It is the latest bombshell allegation to emerge from "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," the book by Charles Spencer, Diana's younger brother, set to hit shelves next week.

In an interview airing this weekend on "CBS Sunday Morning," Spencer explains his explosive allegation that a year after the royal couple's divorce, and with the nation in mourning just after Diana's death at the age of just 36, Charles seemed upbeat.
"Obviously I'm not justifying or criticizing," he told CBS News. "I'm just reporting that's the fact."
Spencer said he believed the then-Prince of Wales' attitude could have been due to him finally feeling free to pursue Camilla, who he later married, and who is now known as Queen Camilla.
"I said in the book that that might have been it, yeah," he told CBS News.

Buckingham Palace pushed back earlier this week after the first allegation from Spencer's book emerged: a claim that Charles had told him days before Diana's funeral that "we'll forget her soon enough."

In a statement unusual in its force for the staid institution, the palace said that while the monarch wouldn't comment directly on a book, he "is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory, even many years after such a loss."

CBS News royal contributor Royya Nikkhah said Thursday that the royal family was in for "a very tricky few days," predicting that Spencer's claims about what the king said after Diana died would be "just the beginning of a serialization that will go on … and we know there are going to be some pretty sensational claims."

"They will have to decide whether or not they're going about each and every claim, or just to make that first response we've heard from the palace their definitive response," said Nikkhah, who is the royal editor for The Sunday Times newspaper. "But it's going to put them into fight mode, and it's going to be very difficult for the king."
Spencer also claims Charles told Diana he didn't love her before their fairy-tale wedding in 1981, and that Diana contemplated suicide more than once.
There has been no further response from Buckingham Palace to the latest claims from Spencer's book, excerpts of which are being published by the Daily Mail tabloid in Britain.

The allegations from Charles Spencer are damaging for King Charles and the royal family, but speaking to people outside Buckingham Palace on Friday morning, CBS News found many who were sympathetic to the monarch.
"I love the king, and I love the royal family," said one man.
A young man, walking with his mother, was less adamant, saying he wasn't "big on the king anyway," but adding that the entire episode, to him, seemed "a shame."

"I'm probably the other way," said his mother. "I probably think it's totally unnecessary and it is just a story at the end of the day. And people are going to believe what they want to believe. But I don't know why it has to keep getting dragged up to be honest."
With five days to go until Spencer's book is available, and more excerpts likely to be published in the interim, it is virtually guaranteed to be dragged up again, and soon.

title: New species of wild cat discovered for first time in more than a century
summary: Scientists have discovered a new species of wild cat for the first time in more than a century, a Bolivian researcher says.
story: Scientists have discovered a new species of wild cat for the first time in more than a century, a Bolivian researcher told AFP on Thursday.
The Tilcayo tiger cat, a small feline with a spotted, leopard-like coat, was identified in the mountainous Yungas region near the capital, La Paz.

Locals who saw the creature in the Bolivian Andes had mistaken it for an ordinary house cat, said biologist and National Geographic explorer Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, who was part of the research team that studied them.
The nickname "tilcayo" given to the animal by locals inspired its new scientific designation: Leopardus tilcayo.
Nogales-Ascarrunz lauded the discovery as a "remarkable event, because a new wild cat species hasn't been described in 100 years."
The cat is the first feline discovered since the Uruguayan pampas cat in 1923.
The tilcayo is slightly smaller than a domestic cat, measuring around 18 inches, with rounded ears.
A pair of tilcayos -- the only such creatures found so far -- have undergone whole genome sequencing, Nogales-Ascarrunz said, referring to a type of in-depth genetic testing.
A male tilcayo is living at an animal shelter in Yungas after it was handed over by a family who had taken it in.
A female was rescued and released into the wild after being attacked by locals.
Research on the species was published on Thursday in the journal Current Biology, capping off research that scientists began in 2021.
"So far, it's only been detected in Bolivia" and not "anywhere else on the planet," Nogales-Ascarrunz said.
She said the creatures were classified as vulnerable to extinction, but their small numbers meant they could soon be considered "at much greater risk" of dying out.

title: Christine Taylor’s ‘Hey Dude’ salary was far lower than castmates remembered
summary: Christine Taylor says her "Hey Dude" salary was just $3,500 per episode, far less than her castmates remembered earning on the Nickelodeon series.
story: The "Ned’s Declassified" alum explains why her tiny residual checks went viral and questions whether Hollywood needs a better system for penny payments. The former child star-turned lawyer is now the host of "Off My Meds."
Christine Taylor is looking back at her early Hollywood career — and revealing that her "Hey Dude" salary was far lower than her castmates remembered.

During an appearance on "The Secret World of Alex Mack" actress Natanya Ross’ "We’re Still Here, Babe" podcast Wednesday, Taylor — who played Melody Hanson on Nickelodeon’s Western comedy series from 1989 to 1991 — said she earned approximately $3,500 per episode by the show’s final season.
"By the time ‘Hey Dude’ ended, we had this discussion among our castmates, and everyone seemed to think [that] by the last season, we were making $5,000 an episode," Taylor said.
Christine Taylor opened up about her "Hey Dude" salary. (WireImage/Getty Images)
"No, we were making $3,500 an episode, I’m pretty sure, because they would bump us up $500 every season," she added.
Taylor said all of the cast members earned the same amount, despite her co-stars’ shared belief that they were making $5,000 per episode.
"Everyone in their brain was like, ‘$5,000.’ I was like, ‘No way, no way. That would have… no, it did not happen,’" she recalled.

The actress said she was careful with the money she earned while working on the popular children’s series. She also credited her family with helping her financially as she moved to Los Angeles and pursued acting.
JENNIE GARTH ADMITS ‘SCARY’ FINANCIAL SPIRAL AFTER ‘90210’ FAME
Taylor starred in "Hey Dude" in the late '80s. (Nickelodeon)
Taylor remembered budgeting closely, using laundromats and monitoring her spending during the early stages of her career.
The actress went on to appear in "Saved by the Bell," "Blossom" and "Robin Hood: Men in Tights" before landing her breakout role as Marcia Brady in "The Brady Bunch Movie."
‘BRADY BUNCH’ STAR SHARES THE SIMPLE WORD THAT SAVED HER FROM HOLLYWOOD TRAPS
Taylor also revealed that she was asked to lose 10 pounds before playing the iconic character in the 1995 film.
"Of course, I was embarrassed when that ask came my way," she said, adding that the request reflected the attitudes of the 1990s and "would never happen today."
FORMER DISNEY STAR DYLAN SPROUSE SAYS ACTING AS A KID WAS ‘CHILD LABOR’

Taylor later starred alongside her husband, Ben Stiller, in films, including "Zoolander" and "DodgeBall." The couple married in 2000, separated in 2017 and later reconciled. They share two children, Ella and Quinlin.

Ben Stiller and Christine Taylor share two children together. (Evan Agostini/AP)

Taylor’s experience is part of a broader pattern in Hollywood, where a recognizable television role does not always guarantee financial security. Several former television stars have revealed that their salaries and residual checks were dramatically different from what audiences assumed.
JODIE SWEETIN SHARES SHOCKING 'FULL HOUSE' RESIDUAL CHECK AMOUNT DESPITE SHOW'S MEGA SUCCESS

"The Sopranos" star Drea de Matteo recently said she was forced to find alternative income after acting work slowed down. The actress revealed that she turned to OnlyFans after facing financial difficulties and a lien on her home.

During an appearance on Jamie Kennedy’s podcast, de Matteo said she earned enough through the platform to pay off a $75,000 lien within 75 minutes of posting a bikini photo. She also said she sometimes earned approximately $100,000 per month.

Drea de Matteo opened up about her second source of income after acting slowed down. (Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images)
"I was not — people think I’m made of f---ing money," de Matteo said. "Everyone sees me coming, they’re like, ‘Here comes that rich b---- from ‘The Sopranos.’ And it’s like, no, I’m not at all."

More recently, "Married... with Children" star Ted McGinley revealed that he receives extremely small residual checks from some of his popular television projects, despite starring in long-running shows.

In an interview with Page Six, McGinley — who also found fame on "Happy Days" and "The Love Boat" throughout the 1970s, ’80s and '90s — said he's holding on to a "whole stack" of checks each worth a total of one penny.
Ted McGinley is seen in New York City on May 2, 2026. (Jason Howard/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)
"I’ve been getting residuals all the time," said McGinley, who admitted the checks become smaller and smaller as the years go by.

title: Aaron Rodgers’ famous exes from Shailene Woodley to the romance that sent him into a 'tailspin'
summary: Aaron Rodgers says he regretted letting now-wife Brittani go years earlier, revealing the secret timeline from their 2017 meeting to their 2025 elopement.
story: Actress Shailene Woodley laughs and keeps walking after being asked whether she has anything to say about ex-fiancé Aaron Rodgers and his recent remarks about their relationship. (BACKGRID)
Aaron Rodgers’ love life has taken him from Hollywood romances and a broken engagement to a secret wedding years in the making.

Rodgers’ road to marriage was anything but a straight line. After high-profile romances with Olivia Munn, Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley, the NFL star ultimately found his way back to the woman he says he regretted letting go years earlier.

The now 42-year-old football star's dating life began drawing celebrity-media attention in the late 2000s and early 2010s. Actress Jessica Szohr was among his earliest well-documented Hollywood connections, but his relationships became substantially more public once he began dating Munn in 2014.
AARON RODGERS MAKES BOMBSHELL CLAIMS ABOUT SHAILENE WOODLEY SPLIT

Aaron Rodgers’ dating history includes high-profile romances with Jessica Szohr, Olivia Munn, Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley, pictured, before he reunited with the woman he calls his "biggest regret" and secretly married in 2025. (Getty Images)
Jessica Szohr

The "Gossip Girl" star and Rodgers had an on-and-off relationship in the early 2010s. Szohr and the quarterback were first linked in 2011, after being spotted publicly together. The former couple initially ended things because of their busy schedules.
The two reportedly rekindled their relationship in 2014 before calling it quits again.
Their romance preceded Rodgers’ more heavily publicized relationships, and the pair appeared to remain on friendly terms afterward.
Jessica Szohr and Aaron Rodgers had an on-again-off-again relationship. (Neilson Barnard/Getty Images)
While there aren't many public details about the couple's rumored relationship, People reported Szohr later attended Rodgers’ birthday party in 2017.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Olivia Munn
Rodgers met Olivia Munn while presenting the Song of the Year award at the ACM Awards in 2014. Their relationship quickly became one of his most high-profile romances.
While both had busy schedules, Munn explained how the two made it work.

"There’s a lot of traveling, a lot of driving, and then you’re just really happy with the decisions that you make. And for me, it comes at a time in my life when I end up having to say no to some work because I gotta be somewhere else. It doesn’t make me sad or anything, because I want my life to be full and have all those experiences, so you kind of figure it out as you go," she told E! News in 2014.
Aaron Rodgers' first high-profile romance was with actress Olivia Munn. (Chris Weeks/Getty Images)
Engagement rumors between the two began to surface in 2016 and Munn even stepped out with a ruby on her ring finger. However, the two called it quits just a few months later.

"When you are living out a relationship in the public eye, it’s definitely… it’s difficult. It has some extra constraints, because you have other opinions about your relationship, how it affects your work and, you know, just some inappropriate connections," Rodgers told ESPN shortly after the breakup.
During their relationship, it became public that Rodgers was estranged from his family, and many of his fans blamed Munn for the rift.
Aaron Rodgers and Olivia Munn arrive at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party in Beverly Hills on Feb. 22, 2015. (Reuters)

"There's this whole big narrative that stayed with me for so many years, but there was just this dynamic in the family that had nothing to do with me. It became this whole big thing, and people were like, 'I can't with her, she's keeping this family apart,'" Munn said during a 2025 appearance on the "Armchair Expert" podcast.

In Ian O'Connor’s 2024 biography "Out of the Darkness: The Mystery of Aaron Rodgers," Rodgers shared that the cause of the schism was "deep-rooted." He also clarified that Munn "had nothing to do all the years" of prior estrangement.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Danica Patrick
Rodgers traded Hollywood glamour for racing royalty when he began dating Danica Patrick.

The former IndyCar and NASCAR star confirmed their romance in January 2018, years after the two had initially crossed paths at the ESPYs. The two had actually kept in touch via email before sparks flew.
Danica Patrick and Aaron Rodgers began dating in 2018. (Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

"We kept in touch a little bit, and there were some years we didn’t talk to each other, and then some every now and again, but it wasn’t until obviously recently that we actually had phone numbers. We referred to each other as Chicago and Green Bay – it was very cute," Patrick told Jenny McCarthy on her SiriusXM show.
The relationship quickly became serious and highly visible, with the pair making public appearances and Rodgers openly discussing their life together.

"We’re just two people who enjoy being around each other and love each other," he told Artful Living in 2018. "We’re really into each other… we’re really attracted to each other… we really enjoy traveling… She’s up for anything travel-wise, which is fun. She’s a good travel partner because she’s so laid-back and low-maintenance. And she’s a hell of a cook, so we love just staying in, too. She eats really healthy. She’s inspired me in that way."
But there would be no trip down the aisle: after more than two years as a couple, Patrick's representative confirmed their split in July 2020.
In a 2025 appearance on "The Sage Steele Show," Patrick spoke about her time with Rodgers, claiming that "the nature of the relationship was emotionally abusive."
Danica Patrick claimed that her relationship with Aaron Rodgers was "emotionally abusive." (Getty Images)

"He leaves a trail of blood," she said, later adding, "It gave me the greatest gift, the greatest gift, which is myself. It gave me the greatest gift of how much I needed to show up for myself and take care of myself."

On a recent episode of "Not Just Football with Cam Heyward," Rodgers shared his side of the story, saying, "I dated Danica. She had just retired. She was depressed and not fun to be around. But I didn’t leave her because I was trying to be there and be a good partner. Then it was going a certain direction, obviously. There was no intimacy; there was nothing."
"She tells a story that she was so blindsided… and that ‘he leaves a trail of blood around him.’ And I’m like, what are you talking about? That is not what happened, by any means."

Shailene Woodley
If Rodgers’ previous romances generated headlines, his whirlwind relationship with Shailene Woodley took things to another level.
Speculation the two were romantically linked first surfaced in 2020, but by February 2021, Rodgers stunned fans by revealing he was engaged while accepting his third NFL MVP award.
Aaron Rodgers and Shailene Woodley first sparked romantic speculation in 2020. (Getty Images)
Woodley soon confirmed she was the mystery fiancée.

But the fairy-tale ending never arrived. Their engagement unraveled, and the pair ultimately separated in 2022 after attempts at reconciliation. The breakup has remained a subject of public discussion: Woodley has spoken about experiencing a deeply difficult period around that time, while Rodgers offered his own sharply different account of their relationship and split in September 2026.

On Heyward's podcast, Rodgers explained that he didn't "ruin" the actress' life during their 2022 split. "I proposed to Shailene and she said yes. Now, she maybe felt like she was forced to make a decision. She could have said no," Rodgers began.
Shailene Woodley and Aaron Rodgers officially called it quits in 2022. (Getty Images)

"A couple days after that, she tells me, 'Before we get married, I gotta go f--- this guy,' and I’m like – because her story is that I ruined her life and gave her crazy depression because I left her. But in actuality, she told me that, and then she took off the ring by March – I proposed in December – and we had a couple of times where we tried to get reunited and nothing ever happened," he said.

"There wasn’t even a relationship in 2022 to break off. She literally told me, 'I don’t want to be with you' after we tried some reconciliation in 2021. There’s just a lot of narrative out there that isn’t true," Rodgers clarified.
Woodley has not responded to Rodgers' claims.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Brittani
After years of very public romances, Rodgers ultimately married someone who has made a point of staying almost completely out of the spotlight.
Rodgers revealed in June 2025 that he was a married man and later identified his wife only as Brittani.

"In 2017, I met my wife, and at the time, she was leaving the States and going back to Europe," he told Heyward on the September podcast. "And my biggest regret is not begging her to stay or proposing right there, because that sent me right there into a tailspin of what can I be accused of as a partner in a relationship."
Aaron Rodgers revealed he married Brittani in 2025. (Michael Owens/Getty Images)

The NFL star explained he met Brittani while she was living in Austin after attending the University of Texas. After the two didn't work out, she moved back to Europe before they reconnected years later.
"She was engaged, then I got engaged, and luckily, for me, we came back together," he said.

The couple quietly eloped in 2025, with Rodgers deliberately keeping his new wife away from the celebrity circus that surrounded his previous relationships. And the notoriously private quarterback is already looking toward their next chapter: Rodgers said in September 2026 that he hopes fatherhood is in his future after football.

title: Alix Earle’s stepmom owns ‘reckless’ past, from Spitzer escort scandal to affair with influencer’s dad
summary: Alix Earle's stepmother Ashley Dupré details her role in the Eliot Spitzer scandal and affair with TJ Earle in a revealing new essay for Elle.
story: Alix Earle talks Super Bowl LX and also gives insight on her upcoming reality show with her sister.
Ashley Dupré isn’t running from her "reckless" past anymore.

Alix Earle’s stepmother opened up about the choices that once made her tabloid fodder, including her connection to the Eliot Spitzer prostitution scandal and her affair with the influencer’s married father. Alix, 25, shot to fame on TikTok and has built a massive following by sharing her life online – including, at times, the complicated family history that played out in the tabloids when she was a child.
Ashley was thrust into the national spotlight in 2008 when she was identified as an escort connected to then-New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer in the prostitution scandal that preceded his resignation.

"At 19, while working as a cocktail waitress, a man approached me and told me I could make $1,000 an hour going on dates with high-profile men," she wrote in an essay for Elle. "My first answer was no, but I kept his card. Eventually, I made the call. I could spend paragraphs explaining why. I was young. I wanted money and independence. I’d spent years operating in survival mode and had become very good at compartmentalizing. But ultimately, I made the call. It was my decision."
ALIX EARLE SPOTTED DANCING WITH TOM BRADY IN ST. BARTS: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT THE SOCIAL MEDIA SENSATION
Ashley Dupré, Alix Earle’s stepmother, opened up about the "reckless" choices that made her tabloid fodder nearly two decades ago. (Getty Images)
According to Ashley, she managed the work for two years without anyone knowing.

"Then, when I was 22, the FBI knocked on my door and showed me a photograph of a man I had seen," she explained. "I didn’t know who he was. When they told me he was the governor of New York, I couldn’t begin to understand what was about to happen."
What followed was a level of attention Ashley said she never could have anticipated.

"Soon, my stage name and face were on the front page of The New York Post. There was an almost ridiculous irony to it," she recalled. "I had come to New York City wanting to be noticed, and suddenly everyone noticed me – for the one thing I never wanted anyone to know."
‘DUCK DYNASTY’ STAR SADIE ROBERTSON HUFF ADMITS ‘FEARS’ OVER PUTTING HER KIDS ON REALITY TV
Ashley Dupré was identified as an escort connected to former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer in the prostitution scandal that preceded Eliot Spitzer’s resignation. (Monica Schipper/Getty Images)
Ashley said she can now look back at that period without minimizing the role she played.

"Context isn’t absolution. I made choices. Some were reckless," she wrote. "Some were selfish. They had consequences. I can own all of that without believing those choices have to be the most interesting thing about me forever."

Ashley's affair with TJ hit the tabloids in 2008, months after she made headline news with the Spitzer scandal. The two had met by chance at a restaurant in New Jersey and things escalated from there. "We talked for five or six hours, and our connection was immediate," Ashley recalled.

"TJ was married," she admitted. "We crossed a line we shouldn’t have crossed, and I take responsibility for my part in that. Our choices affected and hurt other people, including his wife, Alisa, and daughters, Alix and Ashtin, and I don’t take that lightly."
Alix was just a child when the affair turned her family life into tabloid news.

Ashley Dupré also acknowledged her affair with Alix Earle’s married father, TJ Earle, which thrust Alix Earle’s family into the spotlight. (Arnaldo Magnani/Getty Images)

"I remember the day very clearly," Alix said on a 2023 episode of "Call Her Daddy." "Paparazzi had shown up at my house and my mom quickly kind of got me and my sister out of the house over to our cousins. We stayed there for a few days and I had no idea what was going on. I didn't know they were paparazzi. I thought news broadcasters were interviewing the neighbors."
While Alix was too young to understand what was happening at the time, she later discovered who Ashley was.

"It was in like fourth grade," she told host Alex Cooper. "I started to kind of hear commentary from people and I had an iPad at the time. I'm Googling my family and, all of a sudden, I see that the past two years of my life had been a lie."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Alix Earle has previously described the painful impact the scandal had on her childhood and family life. (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for Netflix)

"My dad had an affair with someone who was well-known for her job having sexual relations with high-class people and one of them was even the governor of New York," Alix said. "She was very well-known from that and, in turn, my dad's affair became a very public situation."
Ashley and TJ later married in 2013. But the fallout followed Alix beyond her family’s front door and into her childhood. Friends often weren't allowed to come over to her home.
"The parents would kind of tell my mom, and she would tell me kind of the harsh truth of why this can't happen," she said. "She would have to sit me down and be like, 'They don't really respect us.'"
Behind closed doors, Alix was also grappling with her father's new relationship.

"When my stepmom started to hang around with my dad after he had moved out, she came into his life, and we were introduced to her, which was super weird," Alix explained. "And I was told that I had to be respectful to this woman, and we had to be nice to her. I wanted to rip her head off. It was very weird because I felt like I was a 10-year-old having to be more mature than someone 20, 30 years older than me."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Ashley Dupré, who later married TJ Earle, said she no longer wants to be defined by her past mistakes. (Alexander Tamargo/Getty Images)
Despite their difficult beginning, Ashley eventually became a permanent part of the Earle family. Their relationship evolved in the years that followed, as Ashley and TJ built a life together.
Nearly two decades later, Ashley said she no longer feels the need to convince the world that she is more than her past.
"Twenty years ago, I wanted everyone to understand me. Today, I don’t," Ashley wrote. "The people sitting around my dinner table know who I am. So do I."

"I’m not ashamed of the young woman I was," Ashley added. "I wouldn’t make all of her choices again, but I’m also done wishing her away. She was ambitious, reckless, complicated and sometimes very wrong. But she kept going."

"We live in a culture that can preserve a person’s worst moment forever," she mused. "Accountability matters, but so does allowing people to grow. If we believe that no one can become more than the bad decision they made at 19 or 22, then we leave very little room for any of us to change."

title: Prince Harry’s push to give Archie, Lilibet royal upbringing exposes ‘contradiction’ after palace exit: expert
summary: Prince Harry's children started school in England as experts question whether he can mend the rift with King Charles and Prince William first.
story: British royals expert Hillary Fordwich says Prince Harry is showing signs he wants his children to embrace their English heritage and family roots.
Prince Harry wants his children to embrace their British roots and royal heritage, but one expert says there's a glaring "contradiction."

"Harry spent years telling us why he needed to escape royal life, said his father and brother were trapped, but now appears determined to make sure his children understand and retain their connection to it," Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube's "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital.

"Perhaps with time and distance, he has realized that walking away from royal duties was much easier than walking away from the history, family and identity that came with them," Schofield said. "Ultimately, Harry may finally be recognizing what has always seemed so obvious to the rest of us — being born a prince is an unbelievable privilege."
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle attend the ESPY Awards on July 11, 2024, in Hollywood, California. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have relocated to the U.K. and are eager to teach their two young children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, about their British roots. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for W+P)

On Aug. 20, it was announced that Harry and his wife, Meghan Markle, had decided to return to the U.K. for an extended stay beginning this fall, but they would not resume their roles as working royals. Their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, recently started school in England.

A source told People magazine that Harry "wants them to understand the world he grew up in and where their family comes from." Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell, which handles the offices of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, for comment.

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle pose with their newborn baby son, Archie Harrison Mountbatten-Windsor, in St. George's Hall at Windsor Castle in Windsor, west of London, on May 8, 2019. (Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

"It is totally understandable that Harry wants Archie and Lilibet to grow up appreciating their British heritage, traditions and knowing their extended family," British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "But after all he has said and done, it's highly unlikely the family will ever trust Harry or welcome them all back into the family fold."
WATCH: PRINCE HARRY WANTS HIS CHILDREN TO EMBRACE ENGLISH HERITAGE: EXPERT

"It would have been surprising if he felt California was like home or in any way comparable to anything his children could experience in the U.K.," Fordwich argued. "He has expressed wanting his children to understand their paternal history."

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back as working royals and moved to California more than six years ago. They later signed lucrative contracts with Netflix and Spotify as they sought to become financially independent.

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, Nicole Avant, and Ted Sarandos attend Netflix's BEEF season 2 Montecito Tastemaker at a private residence on April 10, 2026, in Montecito, California. (Stefanie Keenan)

title: Engelbert Humperdinck reveals how an untied shoelace saved his life during British Army service
summary: Engelbert Humperdinck revealed on his podcast how an untied shoelace during British Army training kept him from a deadly assignment in Cyprus.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
British singer Engelbert Humperdinck is reflecting on how his shoelace saved his life during his service in his country's army.

During a recent episode of "The Engelbert Humperdinck Show," the 90-year-old singer reflected on his time in the British Army, sharing that he enlisted in 1954 when he was 18 years old and that an undone shoelace saved his life.
He explained that, prior to being stationed somewhere, he was hoping he would end up in Cyprus because his friend was already stationed there, but he ended up in Germany.

"The way they choose people and when you're in training, you form a rank of threes, and the adjutant goes around with the sergeant major, and he goes counts out 24 people. And they'll say hit Cyprus, Germany, Belgium or whatever it is, wherever you're going to."
ROGER MILLER GIVEN STARK CHOICE AFTER GETTING CAUGHT STEALING: ‘YOU CAN GO TO JAIL OR YOU CAN GO IN THE ARMY’

He took a moment to pause and tie his shoelace, noting that "in the meantime, everybody's forming into ranks of three."

"So I ran after I tied my shoelace and stood where I possibly could in the front line, and they started counting Malaya, Cyprus and I was the next one. Germany. I went to Germany. I was just I just missed Cyprus by one.
"I think God was watching over me because, later on, I found out all the people that went to Cyprus never got there. They got killed in an ambush on the way to Nicosia."

title: Sharon Stone claims ex-husband signed her up for brain surgery without her consent after stroke
summary: Sharon Stone alleges her ex-husband Phil Bronstein signed her up for exploratory brain surgery without her consent after her 2001 stroke.
story: While walking the carpet at the Golden Globe Awards, Sharon Stone told Fox News Digital, ‘You get to choose how you view the world.’
Sharon Stone is opening up about a traumatic time in her life.

She say she never consented to it.
The incident occurred in 2001, after she found herself in a neurological intensive care unit after a subarachnoid hemorrhage and stroke that caused her to go in and out of consciousness.

"First, I woke up, and I was being wheeled to exploratory brain surgery," she said. "He had signed me up for exploratory brain surgery without my knowledge or consent. And I woke up again because the gurney hit something on the floor."

'GAME OF THRONES' STAR EMILIA CLARKE WAS CONVINCED SHE 'CHEATED DEATH' AFTER SURVIVING TWO BRAIN ANEURYSMS

"So, I stood up on the gurney with my hospital gown open, my a-- in the breeze, and suddenly everyone came running — nurses, orderlies, everybody," she said. "And this a--hole doctor, and he had a fax in his hand and he was screaming, 'You can't do that. I'm on the phone with People magazine.'"

She continued arguing with the doctor and telling him she never signed off on that, to which the doctor replied, "Yes, you did. I said you did. And I'm on the phone with People magazine," implying he has told them she is in surgery.

During the interview, Stone also alleged that Bronstein initially delayed taking her to the hospital and then kept telling doctors "that I was faking it."

summary: Carrot Top was hospitalized in Las Vegas, forcing cancellations of his residency shows. His rep says the comedian is recovering and asksed for privacy.
story: Comedian Carrot Top shares his experience on an American Airlines flight in which a woman had a viral meltdown over a ‘not real’ passenger.

title: History-making Miss USA reveals how she got swimsuit-ready while raising 2 young kids
summary: Justus Kelley reveals how she prepped for the Miss USA pageant during nap times and bath routines while caring for her two young foster children.
story: Justus Kelley shares how she practiced with her baby in a carrier, squeezed in workouts during nap time and prepared for the stage around motherhood.
Justus Kelley made history as the first mother and first married woman to win Miss USA, and she got there in an unconventional way.

On Aug. 27, the organization hosted the 75th edition of the national pageant in Miami. The 31-year-old, who was Miss Virginia USA 2026, succeeded last year’s winner, Audrey Eckert, 24. The pageant opened the competition to married women and mothers in 2023.

"My pageant prep, it did look different," Kelley told Fox News Digital. "I'm not going to pretend like I was able to dedicate the same amount of time as what I did in the past. I had to get creative. Their nap time was my prep time. It was late nights.

"It was after the bath and bed routine. I did walking classes with my baby on my chest, in his carrier. I did squats in my living room while holding my 2-year-old. I practiced interview questions while feeding my toddler.
NAVY VETERAN TRADES MILITARY UNIFORM FOR MISS GEORGIA SASH FOLLOWING HEARTBREAKING LOSS

Miss Virginia USA 2026 Justus Kelley is crowned Miss USA 2026 onstage during the 2026 Miss USA Final Competition & Coronation at Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts Aug. 27, 2026, in Miami, Fla. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"There were days when I wished I could just take the entire day to dedicate to pageant prep, but that's not where I am," Kelley said. "That's not the season of life that I'm in. And we made it work, and my family was fully on board with this experience. They know that they're along for the journey; they're along for this ride with me."

The Miss USA pageant began in 1952 in Long Beach, California, with New York's Jackie Loughery becoming its first winner. The competition is separate from the Miss America pageant, which traces its history to a 1921 event in Atlantic City, New Jersey.

Miss USA 2026 winner Justus Kelley and Miss Florida Aileen Cerchiara stand on stage during the 2026 Miss USA Final Competition and Coronation at Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami, Fla., Aug. 27, 2026. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

Kelley, a foster mom of two, is the first married mother to retain the Miss USA title. In 1957, Mary Leona Gage was crowned Miss USA but was stripped of the title the following day after pageant organizers learned she was married and the mother of two sons.
Mary Leona Gage Ennis, who won the title of Miss USA in the contest and then lost it when it was discovered she was married and the mother of two children, is shown in this 1956 photo. (Getty Images)
WATCH: MISS USA 2026 REVEALS HOW SHE TRAINED FOR PAGEANT WITH KIDS IN TOW
Kelley said she ditched social media and TV in favor of workouts whenever she found a spare moment while caring for her two young children.

"I love abductor and adductor exercises, something that I usually do on a machine at the gym," she explained. "But if I can't make it to the gym, I'm just lying on the floor, elevating my leg and mirroring what I would've done on that machine. For me, leading up to a pageant, knowing there's a fitness component, I'm going to be in a swimsuit on that stage. I want to feel good. I want to show off all this hard work.

Abductor and adductor exercises target opposing muscle groups in your hips and thighs that help control side-to-side movement, stabilize your pelvis and support balance and overall lower body stability. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"I really focused on core," she said. "So, a lot of times you'll find me at home in the living room. I might be watching a movie or doing some self-care, but I am on the floor crunching it out during that movie, saying, 'Let's try to get through this whole scene doing crunches,' and then you pause. It was really all about focusing on core."

Miss USA 2026 Justus Kelley stands on stage during the Miss USA Final Competition and Coronation at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami, Fla., Aug. 27, 2026. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)
Kelley said her husband's support also helped her through the competition.

"The crown might be his because all he keeps saying is, 'I can't believe I'm Mr. USA,'" Kelley said with a laugh, referring to her college sweetheart. "I'm like, 'babe, I don't know if that might be trademarked. Stop saying that!'
Justus Kelley and her husband are fostering a baby boy and his sister. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"He is so over the moon," Kelley said. "We've been together for 13, going on 14 years and married for nine. He's been a part of every bit of this journey. I've been competing for over 10 years now. And from my very first pageant, he was there holding a sign with my face on it up until the very end. I did not get here alone. He's been a huge supporter. My husband's a consultant, and he's been calling himself my pageant consultant. But he's been a huge help in getting me to this point."

Justus Kelley walks the runway at the Michael Cinco show during New York Fashion Week Powered by Art Hearts Fashion at The Angel Orensanz Foundation on Sept. 12, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images for Art Hearts Fashion)

This year's prize package, valued at more than $685,000, includes a $150,000 salary, a Range Rover, a one-year lease at a luxury Miami apartment, a Westgate Vacation Home Club membership and a $30,000 Miss Universe wardrobe, according to People magazine.

"The prize that made me go, 'Wow, and I have some questions,' was knowing that the Range Rover is a part of traveling in style even after your year as Miss USA. I think that's huge. But my first question was, 'Does it fit car seats?'"
Miss USA 2026 Justus Kelley wants to raise awareness of providing a loving home to foster children. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)
Kelley said she wants her year as Miss USA to challenge the idea that women need to choose between their families, careers and personal dreams.

Miss Virginia USA 2026 Justus Kelley is crowned Miss USA 2026 onstage during the Miss USA Final Competition & Coronation at Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts Aug. 27, 2026, in Miami, Fla. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"You don't have to choose one part of who you are," Kelley said. "You can be all of who you are. That, to me, is the message. We can embrace every part of who we are. It doesn't take away from the other. It doesn't mean there aren't trade-offs, and there aren't times when we have to lean on our village more heavily to get through all the things that we may be pursuing. But know that we don't have to sacrifice ourselves."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

(L-R) Miss Virginia Justus Kelley, Miss Florida Aileen Cerchiara and Miss Pennsylvania Elizabeth Voight appear on stage during the 2026 Miss USA Final Competition and Coronation at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami, Fla., Aug. 27, 2026. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)
Looking ahead, Kelley said her victory wasn't only personal. She also saw it as a chance to represent mothers and wives balancing family life with their own ambitions.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Justus Kelley and husband Tyler have been licensed foster parents in the Commonwealth of Virginia for nearly two years. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"Knowing that history was made as the first mom, as the first wife, as the first woman in her 30s, my first thought was how amazing it is to get to do this and to represent women from all over the country, from all over the world that resonate with, 'Hey, we're still dreaming,'" she said.

Justus Kelley married her high school sweetheart. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)
"We're raising our families, but we still have dreams. We still have things that we want to go after and pursue. But what an honor. I get to do this. I get to represent these women. What an honor."

title: John Ritter's widow, Amy Yasbeck, details the fatal misdiagnosis she says led to his death
summary: Amy Yasbeck revealed John Ritter was misdiagnosed with a heart attack the night he died, when a CT scan could have detected his aortic dissection.
story: The John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Heath CEO Meredith Ford O'Neal explains why the beloved sitcom star's sudden death resonated with millions and helped raise awareness about aortic dissection.
John Ritter's widow, Amy Yasbeck, is opening up about the actor's final hours more than two decades after his death.
In September 2003, Ritter died at the age of 54 after suffering an acute aortic dissection, a tear in the inner layer of the aorta, the body's largest artery that delivers blood away from the heart.

Ahead of Aortic Dissection Awareness Week and what would have been Ritter's 78th birthday on Sept. 17, Yasbeck, who founded the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health, and the actor's son, Tyler Ritter, who serves on its board, joined Fox News Digital for an interview.
CARLY PEARCE SAYS HEART CONDITION LEFT HER FEARING A HEART ATTACK: ‘IS MY HEART OK?’
John Ritter's widow, Amy Yasbeck, recalled how he was misdiagnosed with a heart attack before dying of an aortic dissection.  (Getty Images)
Looking back on her husband's death, Yasbeck recalled how Ritter was mistakenly treated for a heart attack after arriving at a hospital, which she said "led to what eventually happened."
"John was sadly misdiagnosed on the night he passed away," Yasbeck said.

"And they didn't do any imaging, but he looked like the guy — right age, right weight, everything — to have a heart attack, and he had chest pain," she continued. "So, they just started loading him up with blood thinners and stuff.

"And this is sad because it was the opposite. It wasn't a block in his heart, it was a tear in his aorta, so everything they did that night led to what eventually happened," Yasbeck said. "Because there are ways, once it starts dissecting, if you get to the hospital in time, your chances are way better of living."
John Ritte at CBS TV City Jan. 5, 1978, in Los Angeles. (Tom Wargacki/WireImage)
After Ritter's death, Yasbeck filed a wrongful death lawsuit alleging Ritter's aortic dissection was misdiagnosed. In 2008, a jury found in favor of the two physicians remaining in the case.
WATCH: JOHN RITTER'S DEATH HIT SO HARD BECAUSE ‘YOU FELT LIKE YOU KNEW HIM’: FOUNDATION CEO

To mark Aortic Dissection Awareness Week, which runs from Sept. 13-19, the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health, is launching its "50 for 50" campaign, encouraging supporters to donate $50 while drawing attention to the fact that up to 50% of people who suffer an aortic dissection die before reaching medical care.

Yasbeck told Fox News Digital she believes annual estimates of aortic dissections likely undercount the number of cases because patients who die before arriving at a hospital often are not included in the data. She said that improving awareness of the condition is one of the most effective ways to reduce those deaths.

However, Yasbeck emphasized that raising awareness is not just for patients and families. She pointed out the importance of ensuring doctors recognize that chest pain can signal an aortic dissection, not just a heart attack.
COUNTRY STAR ASHLEY COOKE SPEAKS OUT ABOUT RARE HEART CONDITION THAT COULD END HER LIFE AT ANY MOMENT
Yasbeck founded the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health after the actor's death.  (WireImage)
"Your heart can be in perfect shape," she said. "You can be an athlete.

"And if the blood that's being pumped into your aorta is going inside the layers of the aorta, instead of being traveled to all of the rest of the highway where it's supposed to go, it's curtains for you.

"So, it's so important to be able to have that awareness," Yasbeck added. "And there's no drug for aortic dissection at this point in time. For blood pressure, which sometimes can help you if you are at risk, right? Keep your blood pressure down, but there's no instant fix for it. You have to be a participant in your own health in this regard. And by doing that, you are also protecting your family. For generations, actually."

Yasbeck said she recently witnessed firsthand how her husband's story has become part of emergency medicine. She recalled accompanying a friend with chest pain to the hospital where medical staff told her they were ordering a CT scan to check for "the John Ritter thing" to rule out an aortic dissection.
Yasbeck explained that Ritter's case has become part of emergency medicine.  (FilmMagic, Inc)

"They said, 'We're checking for the John Ritter thing,' not knowing who I am, not knowing whom my friend is that was a friend of John's," she remembered. "It was just like this relief came over me. And my buddy, you know, gave me the thumbs up.

"The fact that they said checking for that ‘John Ritter thing,’ talking shorthand to me, I freaking love that. Call it whatever you want. CT scan, a CAT scan, is the gold standard for diagnosing in an emergency situation, in any situation, but to be able to realize as soon as you can, ‘This is not a heart attack. This is an aortic dissection,’" she continued. "'Fix this a whole different way.'"
'GAME OF THRONES' STAR EMILIA CLARKE WAS CONVINCED SHE 'CHEATED DEATH' AFTER SURVIVING TWO BRAIN ANEURYSMS
While speaking with Fox News Digital, Yasbeck shared that doctors and researchers had told her for years that Ritter's death marked a turning point in awareness of aortic dissection.
"There was kind of a pre-John Ritter awareness of aortic dissection and a post," she said. "Sadly, John died in the last hours of pre-John Ritter awareness."
WATCH: JOHN RITTER'S LEGACY IS HELPING PREVENT DEADY AORTIC DISSECTIONS, DOCTOR SAYS

Since Ritter's death, the "Three's Company" star's family has worked through The John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health to raise awareness about thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections. A thoracic aortic aneurysm is an enlargement of the body's main artery that can often be detected through screening before it tears into an aortic dissection, a life-threatening emergency.

Ritter's widow and his children have encouraged people to learn about their family medical history and seek appropriate screening when they are at increased risk because thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections can have a genetic component.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
John Ritter, with Joyce DeWitt and Suzanne Somers, was known for his role on "Three's Company." (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

Yasbeck said doctors now believe Ritter's father likely died from an undiagnosed aortic dissection, while routine screenings after his death revealed the same condition in his brother Tom, allowing him to undergo life-saving surgery before it became fatal.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Tyler, 41, told Fox News Digital that becoming aware of his family history in the aftermath of his father's death had changed his approach to his own health. Ritter shared Tyler as well as son Jason Ritter, 46, and daughter Carly Ritter, 44, with his first wife, actress Nancy Morgan. Yasbeck, who was Ritter's second wife, shared son Noah Ritter, 28.
Amy Yasbeck, John Ritter, Carly Ritter, Tyler Ritter and Jason Ritter attend the premiere of "101 Dalmatians II: Patch's London Adventure" at El Capitan Theater in Hollywood, Calif. (WireImage)

"It's impossible not to imagine that there's a parallel universe where the family demanded an autopsy on our grandfather and discovered an aortic dissection, which led to my dad and his brother getting screened," Tyler said. "And as we see with Tommy, as Amy just said, Tommy is still alive and doing great.

"It's just too easy to imagine that in this other universe, where my grandfather was properly diagnosed, that my dad would be totally fine right now with just an aortic replacement surgery," he continued. "And that, on the one hand, is very difficult to accept and to comprehend.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"On the other hand, it has provided a massive silver lining," Tyler added. "I get scanned every year. My kids know I get scanned. They know why I get scanned. They know that my dad was the last one in our family. Our mission is that he is the last in our family to suffer a dissection."
Amy Yasbeck and Tyler Ritter attend The John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health's "An Evening From the Heart LA" at Sunset Room Hollywood on May 9, 2024, in Los Angeles. (Getty Images)
Tyler said watching his own children discover their grandfather through episodes of "Three's Company" has reinforced the importance of preserving Ritter's legacy through awareness.

He explained that though aneurysms are often asymptomatic, they can be detected through screening, which is why he encourages families with a history of aortic disease or unexplained early deaths to speak with their doctors.
WATCH: JOHN RITTER FOUNDATION CEO RECALLS SURVIVING LIFE-THREATENING AORTIC DISSECTION
"The more you know," he said. "If you can spot in a first-degree relative that there's a potential for a missed or undiagnosed illness or disease, it would just be worth asking your doctor."
Looking back, Tyler said his father's death remains a tragedy, but one that has helped protect other families.

"It is unfortunate. It's a tragedy," he said. "But it has happened. And, as a result, there are just countless numbers of lives that have been saved."

title: Jennifer Aniston’s romance with Jim Curtis faces celebrity relationship trap, expert warns
summary: Matchmaker Gina Hendrix says Jennifer Aniston may be making classic celebrity relationship mistakes with boyfriend Jim Curtis by trying to build him up.
story: Professional matchmaker Gina Hendrix explains why the 'Friends' star might be making a classic mistake in her relationship.

Jennifer Aniston’s relationship with hypnotherapist and life coach Jim Curtis has gotten serious in the more than a year and a half since they started dating, but a matchmaker worries the "Friends" star could be making classic mistakes as the higher-profile partner.
"I think one of the biggest mistakes is when a woman tries to kind of manage the guy," Los Angeles-based matchmaker Gina Hendrix told Fox News Digital.
"When a woman steps into this role, and it's always a great, successful, amazing woman, she thinks, ‘I did it for myself, I can do it for you too,’ and she tries to build the guy up."

Hendrix warned that the guy often "ends up with all this new great life, but then he resents her for the help, and she takes on a very unsexy role, and then usually it just all fizzles out from there."
JENNIFER ANISTON’S BOYFRIEND, JIM CURTIS, REVEALS WHAT 'FRIENDS' STAR IS REALLY LIKE BEHIND CLOSED DOORS
Jennifer Aniston and Jim Curtis at an event in 2025. (Getty Images for Elle)
She said it takes an "incredibly secure person" to date a celebrity and "share that kind of spotlight but still be out of the spotlight to keep this relationship afloat."

It’s always better to "keep your relationship out of the public eye as much as humanly possible for so many reasons, and if you can live a life where it's under the radar, and you can live a life that is as private as you could possibly have," she added.
THOMAS RHETT REVEALS WHY HE AND WIFE LAUREN REJECT CELEBRITY PERKS FOR COUNTRY LIFE
Hendrix said she appreciates it when celebrity spouses avoid red carpet events.
"You really should just keep it out, keep it away as far as you can" from the public eye, she added.
"I think one of the biggest mistakes is when a woman tries to kind of manage the guy."
WATCH: JENNIFER ANISTON'S ROMANCE WITH JIM CURTIS FACES CELEBRITY RELATIONSHIP TRAP, EXPERT WARNS
MACKENZIE PHILLIPS SHOCKS WITH 15-YEAR CELIBACY CONFESSION AS SHARON STONE, TERI HATCHER RETHINK ROMANCE
Jennifer Aniston interviewed Jim Curtis at an event for his new book earlier this month. (Brie Stimson/Fox News Digital)
MATTHEW MCCONAUGHEY'S PIECE OF RELATIONSHIP ADVICE THAT KEEPS HIS MARRIAGE TO CAMILA ALVES STRONG
The key to a successful relationship involving a celebrity who has "kind of souped up their partner" is "mutual respect," she said.

"You have to be with somebody that, you know, that you want their opinion. You value how they think," she said. "And I think beyond the typical things of attraction and the butterflies in the stomach and the great sex and all these things, you also have to respect this person. And you do have to have a deep friendship because that's really what's going to sustain it way after the looks fade and things start to get ugly, no pun intended."
WORLD SERIES MVP, 'STAR WARS' ACTRESS SHARE HALLMARK-MOVIE LOVE STORY AFTER OVER 20 YEARS OF MARRIAGE

Hendrix said Lady Gaga and fiancé Michael Polansky are a "great example of two people who are living off-grid, living under the radar. And I don't know him, don't know her, but it does seem like that is the route you want to take versus, you know, going on social media with your guy and trying to help build him up."
Jim Curtis and Jennifer Aniston have been increasingly public about their relationship. (Getty Images for Elle)

"Find a man who already has a strong footing, strong boundaries and can kind of be your anchor, not your anchor to pull you down, but your anchor that holds everything in place," she added.
JENNIFER ANISTON, BOYFRIEND JIM CURTIS’ CHEMISTRY SHINES AS SHE REVEALS ‘DEEP FEAR’ DURING INTERVIEW

Speaking specifically about Aniston’s relationship, Hendrix, who clarified that she doesn't know Aniston or Curtis, said, "For whatever reason, she’s decided to sort of help him with his social media."
SYDNEY SWEENEY, SCOOTER BRAUN ROMANCE FACES BIGGEST CHALLENGE YET AS EXPERT WARNS COUPLE TO 'BE PREPARED'

Earlier this week, Hendrix posted a video on her Instagram, saying Aniston was making all the "classic, biggest mistakes" in a relationship involving a woman who is more successful than her partner, especially in trying to bring him up to her level.

Curtis recently told The Sunday Times the "drive" in his relationship with Aniston "was more natural, more organic, less needy. In the past, I’ve felt this idea of, ‘I need you to be in love with me.’ … I wasn’t searching for love anymore. And what do I feel now? I feel real joy, real presence, real calmness, real partnership."
He said in his own life coaching that 82% of his clients are women, attributing that partially to his "nurturing and empathetic" tone.

title: Margot Robbie turns heads in blue bikini on set of new 'Ocean's Eleven' prequel
summary: Photos show Margot Robbie in a 1960s blue bikini filming the "Ocean's Eleven" prequel with Bradley Cooper on location in Saint-Tropez, France.
story: Li Jun Li discussed working with Brad Pitt and Margot Robbie on ‘Babylon,’ saying they were both very kind on set and that Pitt is just as handsome in person as he is on-screen.

"Before Danny Ocean ever stepped foot in Vegas, two masterminds taught him everything he knows — his parents," Robbie said at CinemaCon in July, according to Variety. "You’ll see them in their prime, and, in our new movie, pulling off an epic heist at the 1962 Monaco Grand Prix."
Robbie and Cooper play Danny Ocean's parents in the prequel to "Ocean's Eleven." (The Mega Agency)

title: Duncan Sheik, ‘Barely Breathing’ singer, dead at 56
summary: Duncan Sheik, the voice behind "Barely Breathing" and Tony-winning "Spring Awakening," died from organ failure at 56, his mother confirmed.
story: Singer-songwriter and Tony-winning composer Duncan Sheik speaks with Good Day New York in a 2001 interview about his work in music. Sheik died Sept. 17, 2026, at age 56.
Duncan Sheik, the singer-songwriter behind the hit "Barely Breathing" and the Tony and Grammy-winning musical "Spring Awakening," has died. He was 56.
Sheik died Thursday from organ failure, his mother, Suzanne Sheik, told The New York Times.
Representatives for Sheik did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026: PHOTOS
Duncan Sheik has died. The singer-songwriter was 56. (Gabriela Maj / Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)

"It is with profound sadness that we confirm the passing of Duncan Sheik. The world has a lost a singular talent, and deeply influential voice in music and theater," Sheik’s social media account posted Friday. "Duncan was a father, husband, son, brother, and friend. He will be remembered for his sensitivity, wit, intelligence, and depth of spirit he brought to those who knew and loved him."
The news comes after Sheik’s Instagram account shared an update on his health on Wednesday.

"Barely Breathing" singer Duncan Sheik, who later earned acclaim on Broadway for "Spring Awakening," died from organ failure at age 56, according to his mother. (Margaret Norton / NBCU Photo Bank / NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

"Duncan is currently receiving medical care and remains in critical but stable condition," the statement read. "Out of respect for Duncan and our family, we will not be sharing any further medical details at this time."
"We kindly ask for privacy during this incredibly difficult time and will provide updates when appropriate," the statement continued. "Thank you for the continued love and support."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

The statement was released just before the Off-Broadway premiere of Sheik's new musical, "Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen," and coincided with the announcement of a new Off-Broadway staging of "Spring Awakening."
Duncan Sheik and Steven Sater accept an award for "Spring Awakening" on stage in 2007. (AP Photo/Jeff Christensen)
Throughout the summer of 2026, Sheik frequently posted photos of himself from the hospital on Instagram. He did not publicly share details about his condition.

His song "Barely Breathing," released in 1996, spent 55 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at No. 16. The song earned Sheik a Grammy nomination for best male pop vocal performance in 1998 and later found new audiences on shows including "Glee" and "Girls."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
While "Barely Breathing" made Sheik a familiar voice on ’90s radio, Broadway ultimately became a defining chapter of his career.
The "Spring Awakening" musical was adapted from a 19th-century play by German playwright Frank Wedekind, with music by Sheik and lyrics by playwright Steven Sater.

Lauren "Lolo" Pritchard, Steven Sater, Lea Michele, Jonathan Groff, Duncan Sheik and John Gallagher Jr. attend the premiere of "Spring Awakening: Those You’ve Known" in New York City in April 2022. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
"Spring Awakening" ran for 859 Broadway performances and won eight Tony Awards, including best musical, as well as a Grammy for best musical theater album.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
The original Broadway production helped launch the careers of actors including Jonathan Groff, Lea Michele, John Gallagher Jr. and Gideon Glick.

Sheik later brought his pop background to "American Psycho," which premiered in London before opening on Broadway in 2016. His other projects included "Whisper House," "Legerdemain" and the 2022 album "Claptrap."
Singer-songwriter Duncan Sheik earned a Grammy nomination for "Barely Breathing" before finding major success as a composer for musical theater. (Brian Ach/Invision/AP, File)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Born in Montclair, New Jersey, in 1969, Sheik split his childhood between New Jersey and South Carolina, picking up the guitar at a young age and getting his first synthesizer at 12.
Sheik is survived by his wife, Nora Ariffin, and their 7-year-old daughter, Ines.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Stephanie Giang-Paunon is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Sydney Sweeney’s provocative sports ad 'reinforces the image she has already built' despite backlash: expert
summary: Sydney Sweeney's nude sports trading app ad drew backlash from Olympic athletes, but PR experts say it may not damage her brand at all.
story: Brand expert Adrienne Uthe explains that Sydney Sweeney's provocative ad has competing narratives, as expert says 'perception' can become 'reality.'
Sydney Sweeney sparked widespread backlash following the release of her provocative campaign for a sports trading app.
No stranger to controversy or criticism, Sweeney, 29, faced the music from Olympic athletes, entertainment icons and millions of keyboard warriors who voiced their opinions of the naked ad.

Adrienne Uthe, founder of Kronus Communications, exclusively told Fox News Digital that while Sweeney's latest ad may have ruffled feathers, "women having agency also means allowing women to make choices about their image that other women may not personally agree with."
SYDNEY SWEENEY FIRES BACK AT TROLLS AFTER FACING CRITICISM ONLINE FOR PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD
Sydney Sweeney posed in the nude for her latest campaign, a move that sparked controversy among athletes and experts. (TheStewartofNY)

"People are entitled to dislike the ad, just like women athletes are entitled to criticize it for their own reasons," Uthe said. "But I don't think this is materially damaging to Sydney Sweeney in any way, shape or form.

"In fact, I don't think it's a large departure from who she is and what her brand represents. She's a beautiful woman right now at the peak of her career, and she ultimately can decide which projects she wants to take and which ones she doesn't."
She added, "And she's chosen to make sexuality a part of her brand for better or for worse."
WATCH HERE: EXPERT WEIGHS IN ON SYDNEY SWEENEY PROVOCATIVE AD CONTROVERSY

Sweeney's latest ad featured several shots with strategically placed sports equipment covering her mostly nude body. "Think you know sports? Prove it. Novig is just sports. So, they wanted a show," the "Euphoria" star said in the campaign.
SYDNEY SWEENEY, SCOOTER BRAUN ROMANCE FACES BIGGEST CHALLENGE YET AS EXPERT WARNS COUPLE TO 'BE PREPARED'

Several female athletes didn’t appear to take too kindly to the ad. Australian Olympic gold medalist swimmer Ariarne Titmus, British sprinter Amy Hunt and former American gymnast Gracie Kramer were among those to denounce the ad.
Times Square billboards prominently showed off the provocative Sydney Sweeney ad.  (Anthony Behar/Sipa USA via Reuters Connect)
Sydney Sweeney posed for the Novig sports trading app ad. (Getty Images)
Uthe believed Novig's creative team accomplished its goal, but stressed the significance of effective marketing.
"Going viral tells me they captured attention. It doesn’t tell me they captured the customer," Uthe said.

"This is where social media completely distorts reality, and we've seen this across all platforms in pop culture, politics, sports and beyond. So the narrative that is the loudest isn't necessarily what is true and what the majority opinion is."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Uthe noted that one side claimed the ad objectified women in sports, while the other narrative questions why there's outrage over an obviously provocative ad.
Sydney Sweeney faced the wrath of online critics after posing in a provocative new sports betting campaign. (Carlo Paloni)

"Once one of those frames takes over, whether it's through different content that someone is viewing or someone just inherently has a bias for this topic, that perception is really gonna make it a reality for them," Uthe said. "And that's why I always say, if you can make it trend, you can it true."
Olivia Bennett, senior account director at Go Up, thought that the campaign was simply "bad for women in sport."

"I can understand the commercial calculation behind choosing Sydney Sweeney," Bennett told Fox News Digital. "Novig will know its audience, and Sydney has built a public brand where sex appeal, provocation and controversy consistently generate attention.

"But this was a national campaign. When you choose someone with such a heavily sexualized and frequently controversial public image, you know the campaign is going to travel far beyond your existing customer base. The wider reaction was entirely foreseeable."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Bennett believed that the bigger issue at hand was what the ad said about women in sports.
"What I find most telling is that female athletes themselves are now pushing back and saying: this isn’t how we want women in sport to be represented," she said.
Sydney Sweeney said that the ad was intended to "cut through the noise and put the focus entirely on sports." (Getty Images for Stagecoach)
"Once the people who actually work and compete in that world start using your campaign as an example of the problem, you have a much bigger reputational issue than a few negative comments online."

She added, "For Sydney, I don’t think the campaign is off-brand at all. If anything, it reinforces the image she has already built. But that doesn’t make it good for women in sport. Personal-brand fit doesn’t remove the wider impact of the message you’re putting into the world."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

In what appeared to be a response to the backlash, Sweeney shared a number of ESPN magazine covers featuring nude athletes, including Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Caroline Wozniacki.
"It's gamedayyyy," the blonde bombshell wrote before tagging the newly launched sports platform.
Sydney Sweeney expanded her business portfolio with the launch of lingerie brand SYRN earlier this year. (Getty Images)
While many comments encouraged "The Housemaid" actress, Sweeney was hit with accusations of sexualizing a predominantly male-dominated field.

"As a former athlete and a woman who has personally experienced sexualized comments, I’m genuinely disgusted and deeply disappointed by this campaign," one user wrote. "We’ve spent years fighting to be seen and respected for our talent, strength, and achievements-not reduced to our bodies."

"The campaign was about embracing a fun idea," Sweeney said in a statement, according to Variety. "The concept is simple: cut through the noise and put the focus entirely on sports. The campaign brings that idea to life with confidence, humor and a playful edge."
